Definition: from G53; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally):--purify (self).
BiblicalUsage: The word hagnízō carries the sense of purify (self). In John 11:55, the text says "to purify themselves." In Acts 21:24, the text says "and purify thyself with them."
TheologicalSignificance: What hagnízō teaches me is that purity is not prudishness; it is keeping ourselves for the God who made us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Raising of Lazarus; Paul Purifies Himself at the Temple
